question: Can consolidating Hungarian-cost transfers make the unchanged object planner practical while preserving numerical decisions?
hypothesis: One host copy of all cost matrices can reduce synchronization overhead. Batched index transfer/reduction may further help; model rollout may instead dominate and improvements may be insufficient.

sources.consequence: CPU/GPU copies synchronize. Batch tiny transfers where numerical behavior is preserved; synchronize before/after timing. Per-task saved latency already includes terminal host-side cost/actions.
Retain minimum full assignment with identical cost matrices; square assignment rows are sorted. Consolidating transfers must not change matching objective or CEM decisions.
Batching reductions may change rounding. Preserve full64 model policy and require direct cost, rank, action and physical score agreement before any new planning runtime.
Retain original local B001 CEM candidates/elites/iterations/seeds and Hungarian latent-goal objective. Runtime improvement is not planner tuning or a scientific result.

differences: Operational/runtime optimization only outside frozen go2nav sources and four reviewed C009v2 helpers. contrary_evidence: Transfer overhead may be a small fraction; full64 transformer rollout can dominate. Reduction regrouping can change near-tied ranks and CEM trajectories. Prefix throughput does not guarantee full completion, and an insufficient speedup must remain a technical/resource finding.
